notes.title: Devlog #4 - From the DEV
notes.notes:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42288265/1851ce8ca64ddde3027d8a3b522e9043bc1f2b1f.png[/img]

Hi, this is the developer of [b]HACKERGAME[/b].

I would like to give you those who are interested in the technical side of the job, unlike this designer guy I don't have fancy words and banners.

We used to use Unity as a game engine but as we continued in the development process, we came across a lot of roadblocks and challenges posed by Unity, this is why we are going to switch to the unpopular way of creating games.

We are going to develop our game based on Electron with React, .Net API with SignalR, Mediator and SQLite.

I know it might sound crazy to do that but some of the biggest challenges were reactivity, styling and maintainability of the code, I wasn't able to deliver applications as they were in designs or I would have to spend a lot more time than I should.
[b]Skill issue I guess ¯\_(ツ)_/¯[/b]

You might think why .Net though, isn't Electron and React enough but there is a reality that .Net is easier to work with and has more functionality when it comes to connecting local DB and doing other actions with it.

In this way, we are hoping our project will have a much better-looking UI and cleaner code with richer content.
[i]famous last words...[/i]

So that's all for this Devlog episode. If you have any questions or suggestions, you can join our [url=https://discord.gg/PVEvxfbN8w]Discord[/url]. and let us know. Have a nice day.

I am going to drop some spoilers to show you how much our UI will improve in the next DevLogs.

Regards,
The DEV

notes.title: Devlog #3 - Breacher Framework
notes.notes:
[h2][b]The backbone of the toolset. Breacher Framework.[/b][/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42288265/0da664483ec988272fd0902e64a0bf34c28dbfa0.png[/img]

Breacher Framework, or BRC for short, is one of the main tools that you will be using in the HACKERGAME to perform cyberattacks. I mostly inspired it from [url=https://www.metasploit.com]Metasploit Framework[/url] and made it highly simplified. At the current state of BRC, there are two modules. These are; 

porthack - Deploys a reverse shell on vulnerable targets.

uploadx - Generates an exploit for file upload vulnerabilities.

I plan to add more modules further into development. The one module I planned to add right now is Remote Desktop Control. We haven't designed or coded it yet. But when it's added, you will be able to connect target computers, see its desktop and control it from the screen. (Hopefully)

For now, let's focus on the existing modules. Starting with 'porthack', if you have played [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/365450/Hacknet/]Hacknet[/url] -which is our main inspiration to make HACKERGAME- It will sound similar since the name is exactly the same. And it actually does almost the same thing. If you disable enough ports, you can use porthack to infiltrate the target. It's quite simple. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42288265/98ee4668174276d415940993074d06155ef26fa3.png[/img]

As for the uploadx, not all of the systems are hackable through port hacking. Some have updated security and have no vulnerabilities. So this is where you can try your luck with the File Upload Exploits. For this one, I've inspired from another real life tool called [url=https://www.kali.org/tools/weevely/]Weevely[/url]. 

Using the uploadx module; you can create a reverse shell in '.php' or a '.png.exe', monitor the upload page to obtain the uploaded location on the server and finally, execute the shell. You can check out the screenshot below, it kinda gives an example. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42288265/4746cdb37f5a1595287eecb9b896fb872f87aae6.png[/img]

So that's all for this Devlog episode. If you have any questions or suggestions, you can join our [url=https://discord.gg/PVEvxfbN8w]Discord[/url]. and let us know. Have a nice day.

notes.title: Devlog #2 - A Digital Nightclub
notes.notes:
[h2][b]Electronic music, data trafficking, and unfiltered chat. Welcome to the Club Decagon. [/b][/h2]

I'm trying to create a little nightclub-themed illegal chatting platform just like you see in the movies, where two guys talk in a loud club about some shady business. In Club Decagon, you will be doing similar things, talking about some stolen data or a hacked server, or you will be the one who recieves the mission and going after the targets. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42288265/1e38f76104b7de7635fbbca4b15c485c027d4d48.png[/img]

Even tough Club Decagon won't be a big part of the game, I still think it's a great little idea to add into the HACKERGAME universe.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42288265/118f182cf3b76adc7eec886c62a7bbba453f870d.png[/img]

 Let us know if you have any questions or suggestions for HACKERGAME. You can also reach us from [url=https://discord.gg/PVEvxfbN8w]Discord[/url].

notes.title: Devlog #1 - Network Analysis Tool
notes.notes:
[h1]Hello and welcome to HACKERGAME Devlogs.[/h1] I've been wanting to share some of the development processes of HACKERGAME with those who are curious about the game's current status for a while. I am hoping that this devlog series will satisfy you. So let's begin;

The first network analysis tool we created was also used to hack the target networks, which was almost 70% percent of the game. Even though HACKERGAME is an arcade experience, we didn't want all the hacking to be done through one single software. 

If you've seen the old screenshots of HACKERGAME on the steam page, then you've probably seen the old TARGTR interface. For those who have missed it, here is a photo of it:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42288265/fad7f05ebc4c2de86c678c6bd211c7953af92b3f.jpg[/img]

TARGTR's purpose was to both scan the target ports and attack them with built-in exploits. Like Nmap combined with Metasploit. But as I said, this gameplay mechanic was way too arcade and wasn't fun at all. So we've removed the hacking option from TARGTR and made it only for information-gathering purposes. With this change, I've redesigned the UI of TARGTR. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42288265/a7205cb6ab960292771e850dcbba84beefdb6341.png[/img]

The original TARGTR works directly on the terminal without any user interface, the version you see above will be available further into the game. But of course, using or not using it will be completely up to you. If you like things in a more old-fashioned way, you can keep on using the terminal version.



So this is it for this Devlog episode. Let us know if you have any questions or suggestions for HACKERGAME. You can also reach us from [url=https://discord.gg/PVEvxfbN8w]Discord[/url].
